## Action

**Use the predicted 33rd-percentile auction price (q33) to screen watches for further investigation—not to make automatic purchase or bidding decisions.**

- Compare the model's q33 of the **recorded USD sale price** with the catalogue estimate range. The file does not record when that estimate was published.
- Flag a candidate when `predicted q33 ≥ 1.10 × benchmark`.
- Treat the **10% margin as illustrative**, not an optimized trading threshold.
- Without a documented pre-auction benchmark, **report the estimate without a flag**.

::: {.notes}
Our objective is to prioritize further review. We cannot claim profitable purchase decisions because the historical dataset does not establish executable pre-auction costs, resale proceeds, or investigation expenses.
:::

## Reason

**The five-feature gradient booster has 20.30% lower 2024 validation dollar pinball than linear quantile regression.**

| 2024 validation (802 watches) | Mean dollar pinball | Share at or below q33 |
|:--|--:|--:|
| Linear q33 | $3,975.74 | 30.42% |
| **Gradient booster** | **$3,168.73** | **35.41%** |
| Reduction | **$807.01 (20.30%)** | — |

- Predictors stay brand, model, case material, movement, and age at sale.
- **None of the tested feature bundles improved** that 2024 dollar pinball.
- IQN ($3,207.60) and CatBoost ($3,321.24) were not selected. Both have higher 2024 pinball.
- 2025–2026 is a later window, not an untouched holdout.

::: {.notes}
Pinball is the 2:1 loss divided by 3. Overestimation costs twice underestimation. The booster was not retuned after the later windows. Feature groups B through F all had higher 2024 pinball than $3,168.73, and their date-clustered intervals included zero.
:::

## Risk

**Lower pinball is not the same as a quantile that sits near one third, and the recorded price is not a verified hammer.**

- In 2026, **23.80%** of sales fell at or below the booster q33. The target is **33.33%**. The quantile sat too low.
- The linear model that year is closer, at 28.95%, but its pinball is higher: $6,537.68 against $5,540.14.
- Rolex is the costly slice: booster share 21.40% versus linear 31.69%, while booster pinball is lower by $1,802.08. We kept the booster because pinball is the decision loss.
- The separate interval, adjusted by **$650.96** from 2023 only, covered **78.43%** of 2024 sales and **72.65%** of 2026 sales, against 80%. That adjustment does not change q33.
- Two public Bonhams lots label the recorded amount "inc. premium." The screen compares a prediction of that recorded price with a catalogue estimate. It flags a lot for investigation. It does not show a profit.

::: {.notes}
A share below 33.33% means the predicted q33 was too low, so a 10% screen flags fewer watches. That is the less costly error under the 2:1 loss, and it is still a failed calibration claim for 2026 Rolex and Cartier. We would switch if a later Rolex window put the booster's pinball above the linear model's, or if the team decided a share near 33% outranks pinball.
:::

## Value

**The measured gain is $807.01 less pinball per 2024 validation watch. That is not a trading return.**

- The 20.30% reduction is $3,975.74 − $3,168.73.
- The same five-feature booster stays ahead of the linear model on pinball in every fixed-setting year from 2022 through 2026.
- Added listing attributes did not improve the 2024 score, and their publication time is not in the file.
- A sale above the catalogue midpoint is not evidence the flag would have made money. The file has no bid, purchase, or resale.

::: {.notes}
Do not multiply $807.01 by the number of watches and call the result profit. The price-basis audit did not redefine the target. If the team later decides the target should be the hammer rather than the premium-inclusive sale price, the ranking has to be recomputed before the 20.30% figure is reused.
:::
